en.title: Insert the Fewest Integers to Eliminate All Zero-Sum Segments
en.description:
You may only insert arbitrary integers into the original array; original elements cannot be deleted or changed. Make the sum of every non-empty contiguous segment nonzero, and find the minimum number of insertions. If the original array contains 0, the single-element zero segment cannot be eliminated, and this site's convention is to output −1 for no solution.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n integers. The source gives no value bounds; this site sets 1≤n≤200000 and elements in −10^9..10^9.
en.explanation: Example 1: inserting 100 after 3 leaves no zero-sum segment, so at least one insertion is needed; the answer is 1. Example 2: every adjacent pair of opposite signs sums to 0, so one insertion is needed in each of the three gaps; the answer is 3. Example 3: the original element 0 is always a zero-sum single-element segment, so there is no solution: −1.
hints: Scan while keeping the set of prefix sums of the current unseparated segment. If adding the current item repeats a prefix sum, insert a separator before the current item and start a new segment containing only the current item.
